title: embeddings-rerank-incident-scratch-ayan-verma-2026-03-13
content:
Quick scratchpad for the embeddings->rerank anomaly we're chasing. Mostly notes-to-self + commands/log snippets. Sharing with Maya/Evelyn for context.

Summary:
- Customers observed intermittent 400s from /v1/rerank and high tail latency around 2026-03-10 18:00 -> 2026-03-12 04:00 UTC.
- Two distinct failure modes surfaced: 1) dimension mismatch errors when ingesting embeddings from upstream (client or preprocessing step changed embedding model/dim); 2) latency spikes (p95 up to ~1.2s for single-item rerank) correlated with batching/backpressure on the rerank worker.
- Repro, small tests, and logs below. Hypotheses prioritized at bottom.

Timeline (rough):
- 2026-03-10 17:45 UTC: spike alert on rerank p95 (from 180ms -> 1.2s).
- 2026-03-10 18:12 UTC: first customer report: 400s with body "embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024".
- 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC: Canary deploy rolled out quantization/compile change for embedding-model v2 (notes in PR #678).
- 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC: some jobs started reporting slow KV cache warmups on rerank workers.
- 2026-03-12 08:00 UTC: partial rollback on compile change (hotfix) but incidents still sporadic.

Commands I ran locally to reproduce (internal endpoints):
- curl to rerank endpoint (force small batch):
  curl -X POST "https://api.internal.redwood/re-rank/v1/rerank" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query_embedding": [0.0, 0.1, ...], "candidate_embeddings": [[...]], "candidate_ids": ["c1"] }'
  -> got: 400 {"error":"InvalidArgumentError", "detail":"embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024"}  (consistent)

- python quick check sending generated embeddings with different dims:
  from requests import post
  url = 'https://api.internal.redwood/re-rank/v1/rerank'
  payload = {"query_embedding": [0.0]*1536, "candidate_embeddings": [[0.0]*1536], "candidate_ids": ["c1"]}
  r = post(url, json=payload, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {TOKEN}"})
  r.status_code -> 200 (works)

  payload2 = {"query_embedding": [0.0]*1024, "candidate_embeddings": [[0.0]*1024], "candidate_ids": ["c1"]}
  -> 400 Dimension mismatch (expected 1536)

Logs / error snippets (pulled from rerank-service logs):
- 2026-03-10T18:11:57Z ERROR rerank.handler - payload validation failed: "InvalidArgumentError: embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536, got 1024" stack=...
- 2026-03-11T02:37:22Z WARN rerank.worker - batch queue backlog=82, avg-process-ms=420, kv-cache-hit=false
- 2026-03-11T02:38:02Z ERROR rerank.worker - latency spike processing batch id=abc123 p95=1183ms root_cause=kv_cache_warmup

Observations:
- Dimension mismatch appears to be coming from a downstream client or the embeddings pipeline switching model. Most prod traffic expects 1536-length embeddings (we onboarded text-embed-1536-svc last year). Some customers/clients are sending 1024 vectors (text-embed-1024 legacy or open-source variant). Rerank endpoint validates vector length strictly and returns 400.
- Latency spikes correlate with high batch queue depth and KV cache misses (worker restarted or cold start). When kv-cache-hit=false in logs, p95 jumps.
- Canary deploy of model compile/quantization may have increased cold start time for some allocs; check rollout windows and instance churn around 2026-03-11 02:30 UTC.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Client/ingest changed embedding model without updating rerank config. Need to identify offending customer keys and fallback policy. Quick fix: add a lenient acceptance path that auto-detects dim and routes to appropriate scorer (or returns 422 with clearer message).
2) Canary compile changed startup latency -> increased cold starts -> KV cache warmups -> tail latency. Need to correlate instance restart events with timeline.
3) Batching/backpressure interaction: when batches get big, scorer does synchronous work causing head-of-line blocking. Potential mitigation: max-batch-size on worker, adaptive batching.

Repro steps (to validate each hypothesis):
- H1 (dim mismatch): search logs for "embedding vector length mismatch" and map to api_key/customer. Query auth logs -> identify which client started sending 1024 vectors.
  commands: grep -R "embedding vector length mismatch" /var/log/rerank/*.log | sed -n '1,200p'
- H2 (cold starts): cross-check k8s events + deploy times. kubectl get events for namespace rerank-prod around 2026-03-11 02:00-03:00 UTC. Check instance creation timestamps in autoscaler logs.
- H3 (batching): ramp load in staging, force backlog by sending many simultaneous small requests and measure p50/p95. Use loader script: locust / wrk with concurrency 200 hitting rerank with valid 1536 vectors.

Temporary/workaround actions taken so far:
- Rolled back the quantization compile in the canary (partial) -> reduced instance churn but didn't eliminate errors.
- Added more logging around embedding dims accepted (PR #679) to capture api_key/customer and dimension at ingestion time (deployed to staging).
- Notified CS to contact customers if we identify keys producing 1024 embeddings.

Data points / metrics observed (from dashboard snapshot):
- rerank p50: baseline 180ms -> spike 420ms during incident window
- rerank p95: baseline 520ms -> spike 1183ms
- error rate (4xx): rose from 0.2% -> 2.4% (mostly 400s dimension mismatch)
- kv-cache hit rate: dropped from 92% -> 41% during spike windows

Open questions / things to confirm:
- Which embedding model(s) should be the single source of truth for rerank (1536 vs 1024)? Is there an existing migration doc? Product/Docs? (ping product-hosted-api).
- Do we want rerank to accept multiple dims and internally map to a canonical space (e.g., re-embed or pad/truncate)? Tradeoffs: cost + correctness.
- Did the canary change modify scheduling affinity so instances were rebalanced across racks/azs increasing cold starts? Check rollout policy settings.

Next steps (short-term):
- Run grep/audit to map api_keys -> dims (priority). If we can identify clients, CS outreach + temporary schema enforcement on client side.
- Add dimension-acceptance telemetry to prod (log aggregated counts by dim).
- Investigate autoscaler events and canary rollout metadata (who triggered, which commits). See INF-2142.
- Implement a defensive server change: clearer 422 with suggested remediation and link to docs; 2-day hotfix window.

Notes to self (random):
- Sample mismatch stack: InvalidArgumentError: Embedding vector length mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1024 at rerank/scorer.py:88
- Candidate quick fix for multi-dim: if dim == 1024 -> run a 1024->1536 projection model (cheap MLP) before scoring. Explore quality impact on ranking.

Useful links:
- Jira: INF-2142 (incident)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/re-rank-service/pull/678 (compile change)
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/rerank-prod/overview?from=2026-03-10T16:00:00Z&to=2026-03-12T10:00:00Z

If anyone hits this doc, feel free to leave quick notes here. I'll follow up with a short post-mortem draft after we close the loop on clients and the canary rollback.

-- Ayan
